A Bicycle is defined as a human powered device with 2
wheels bigger than 16 inches.

Bicycles must obey traffic lights and stop signs (as well
as all other traffic control devices).
Bicycles & Pedestrians must follow traffic laws.
Bicycles cannot ride on some limited access highways.

Bikes
forbidden:

SR 520, I-405, I-90 (exit 0 to exit 17), I-5 (Lakewood
to Marysville), parts of 18, 518, 522 & 599 and a few
others.

A bicycle must yield to a pedestrian on a sidewalk or
crosswalk.
Parents are responsible for kids obeying bike laws
Mopeds and gas powered bikes & scooters are not

allowed on sidewalks or trails.
Electric-assist bicycles are not allowed on sidewalks.
Electric-assist bicycles may be allowed on multipurpose
trails, but may be restricted based on local jurisdiction
regulation.
Only one person per bicycle seat.

Bicycles may use the shoulder of the roadway or any
specially designated bicycle lane if such exists.

Bicycles should ride as near to the right side of the right
through lane as is safe except when turning or passing
another bicycle or vehicle proceeding in the same
direction.
Bicycles can ride on the left side of the left through lane
as is safe (with the traffic flow) on one way streets.
